changes.before: Implement lookupQuery(id). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Keep the SQL instructions fixed and supply the requested ID separately.

before: A bound query keeps the SQL structure fixed while supplying values separately. User text must not become part of the SQL program.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
The question mark is a value placeholder. params holds the value to bind through a database API. Returning this object does not execute SQL; the adapter must actually use parameter binding.

Read the function call lookupQuery("7") from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, lookupQuery runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
What happens to the text "7 OR 1=1" in this query model? The SQL text stays fixed. A correctly binding database adapter treats the parameter as data.
after: SQL instructions tell a database what to do. Caller-supplied text should stay data, not become more instructions. A bound query keeps the SQL text and its input values separate.
A placeholder marks where a value belongs. Here, ? is the placeholder, and params is an array holding the ID to supply. Binding means giving that value to the database through its parameter API.
Even text containing SQL-like words stays one parameter value. Do not rewrite the SQL string by joining the supplied ID into it.
This function only describes the query. It does not run it. The database adapter must use actual parameter binding; joining the values into SQL later would undo the separation.
Complete lookupQuery(id). Return the exact shown SELECT text and params containing the supplied ID. Keep the input's value and type unchanged.

changes.before: Runs as a pure JavaScript function in the browser. Passing checks does not establish live HTTP behavior, database durability, concurrency safety, authentication security, queue delivery guarantees, or production readiness.
changes.after: This browser exercise builds a query description. Real SQL safety depends on the database adapter using parameter binding when it executes the query.
